# README visuals: source

Everything under [`../assets`](../assets) is generated by the code in this folder. Nothing is drawn by hand
and nothing is fetched from an image host, so every visual can be changed, reviewed and rebuilt like code.

## What is here

| Path | Produces |
|---|---|
| `lib/core.mjs` | Palette, outlined typography, the official logo geometry, shared backdrop and helpers |
| `lib/wordmark.path.txt` | The wordmark outline, traced from the official logo artwork |
| `scenes/hero.mjs` | `banners/hero.svg`: the animated title sequence |
| `scenes/brand.mjs` | `brand/*.svg`, `banners/footer.svg`, `diagrams/divider.svg` |
| `scenes/architecture.mjs` | `motion/architecture.svg`: the exploded isometric system stack |
| `scenes/pipeline.mjs` | `motion/pipeline.svg`: a posting travelling through the job pipeline |
| `scenes/matching.mjs` | `motion/match-engine.svg`: the seven-factor score in two acts |
| `scenes/journey.mjs` | `motion/journey.svg`: who does what, as a swimlane |
| `scenes/features.mjs` | `features/*.svg`: the six capability cards |
| `capture/capture.mjs` | Real screenshots from a running instance in demo mode |
| `capture/tour.mjs`, `capture/compose_tour.py` | `motion/product-tour.gif` from those screenshots |
| `capture/stills.py`, `render-stills.mjs` | WebP screenshots, the phone composite, `hero-static.webp`, `social-preview.jpg` |

## Rebuilding

Requirements: Node 20+, Python 3 with Pillow, FFmpeg, and a Playwright Chromium (set `CHROMIUM_PATH` if
it is not found automatically).

```bash
cd .github/assets-src
npm install
npm run build                 # every vector asset (or: node build.mjs hero)

# Screenshots need the app running in demo mode (no Supabase variables) in another terminal:
#   npm run dev   (from the repository root)
OPS_PATH=<operations console route> npm run capture
npm run tour                  # product-tour.gif
npm run stills                # WebP screenshots, static hero, social preview
```

`OPS_PATH` is the operations console's route; it is read from the environment so it is not written into
the repository's documentation. Without it the operations screens are skipped.

## How the motion works on GitHub

GitHub shows README images through `<img>`, which runs no scripts and loads no web fonts. So:

- **Animated SVGs use CSS keyframes and SMIL only.** No JavaScript, no external references.
- **All text is outlined into paths at build time** (Inter Tight, Instrument Serif and JetBrains Mono, all
  under the SIL Open Font License), so the typography is identical on every platform. Glyphs are defined
  once per file and placed with `<use>` to keep files small.
- **Every animated element's base style is its finished state.** A viewer that ignores CSS animation still
  shows the complete composition, and `prefers-reduced-motion` turns the motion off.
- **Each loop returns to its first frame**, so the animations repeat without a visible jump.
- **The product tour is a GIF** because it is built from screenshots. It holds still between scenes and only
  the spotlight's arrival changes pixels, which keeps it near 3.5 MB.
- **Assets sit on dark cards with their own background**, so they read the same in GitHub's light and dark themes.

## The logo

The mark's three shards are exact polygons fitted to the official artwork, and the wordmark is a trace of
the same file, kept in the artwork's own coordinate space so the proportions are unchanged. On dark
backgrounds only the wordmark's colour is inverted, from charcoal (`#1E1E1E`) to warm white (`#F4F1EC`).
The ember (`#F95135`) is measured from the artwork.

| Token | Value | Use |
|---|---|---|
| Ember | `#F95135` | The mark, primary accents, "AI and engine" in diagrams |
| Ember light / Amber | `#FF7A52` / `#FFB98A` | Gradients, highlights, the serif accent line |
| Ink | `#1E1E1E` | The wordmark on light backgrounds |
| Paper | `#F4F1EC` | The wordmark and text on dark backgrounds |
| Sky | `#7CC6EE` | "A person did this": specialist steps, responses |
| Night | `#07080B` to `#0D1015` | Backgrounds |
